analyzed_vuln.description: `new_object` mishandles a DXF group-code 310 value when parsing an entity outside the guarded `AcDbEntity` preview path. The generic common-field loop matches code 310 to the malloc-owned common `preview` (`TF`) field and calls `dwg_dynapi_common_set_value(_obj, f->name, &pair->value, 1)`. For this non-string pointer field the dynapi setter only copies the `pair->value.s` pointer, rather than the data. `new_object` then reaches `next_pair` and `dxf_free_pair` frees that same string/binary allocation, leaving `entity->preview` dangling. Later `dwg_free_common_entity_data` frees `preview` again, producing the reported double-free. The caller must route all valid 310 preview data through `add_ent_preview`, reject it, or explicitly transfer/copy ownership before freeing the pair.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A crafted DXF is read through `dwg_read_dxf` and creates a POINTCLOUD entity (the PoV places it in the BLOCKS data). It supplies a group-code 310 binary/string pair while the current subclass/parsing state does not satisfy the special preview condition (`is_entity`, no prior preview size, fixed type above LAYOUT, and subclass exactly `AcDbEntity`). The generic common-entity lookup still recognizes 310 as the `preview` field, aliases the pair-owned allocation into the entity, and the normal `dxf_free_pair` cleanup frees it. A subsequent `dwg_free` of the partially/malformed-but-retained POINTCLOUD entity attempts to free the dangling preview pointer a second time.

patch_result.patch:
--- a/libredwg/src/in_dxf.c
+++ b/libredwg/src/in_dxf.c
@@ -11714,15 +11714,17 @@
                           pair = add_ent_preview (obj, dat, pair);
                           goto start_loop;
                         }
-                      else if (pair->code == 310 && is_entity
-                               && obj->tio.entity->preview_size
-                               && obj->fixedtype > DWG_TYPE_LAYOUT
-                               && strEQc (subclass, "AcDbEntity"))
+                      else if (pair->code == 310 && is_entity)
                         {
-                          // This would corrupt the previous preview chain,
-                          // don't append
-                          LOG_ERROR ("Skip duplicate/interrupted %s.preview",
-                                     obj->name)
+                          // All valid common entity preview data is consumed by
+                          // add_ent_preview above.  Never pass another 310 to
+                          // the generic setter: preview is malloc-owned while
+                          // the pair value is freed at next_pair.
+                          if (obj->tio.entity->preview_size)
+                            LOG_ERROR ("Skip duplicate/interrupted %s.preview",
+                                       obj->name)
+                          else
+                            LOG_WARN ("Skip out-of-state %s.preview", obj->name)
                           goto next_pair;
                         }
                       else

args: In src/in_dxf.c, analyze new_object's handling of DXF group code 310 and the common entity preview field. Identify the exact generic-field branch that aliases pair->value.s into entity->preview, explain the special add_ent_preview path and pair ownership, and recommend the smallest root-cause fix that preserves valid preview parsing while ensuring every code-310 pair outside the valid preview state cannot reach the generic dynapi setter.

The supplied ASan report shows a POINTCLOUD parsed in BLOCKS receives group code 310 while the subclass is not exactly AcDbEntity. The special preview branch is skipped, then common-field lookup finds malloc-owned TF field preview and dwg_dynapi_common_set_value copies the pair-owned pointer. new_object later invokes dxf_free_pair around line 12032, and dwg_free_common_entity_data frees the dangling preview pointer. I am considering intercepting code 310 for all entities before generic common-field lookup: valid AcDbEntity preview chunks should still call add_ent_preview, while invalid/out-of-state chunks should be ignored/rejected and then normally pair-freed. Please inspect relevant control flow and any implications such as subclass matching, preview_size, fixedtype, and whether code 310 has legitimate non-preview meanings in object-specific parsing.
